root_cause.text: The ksmbd auth functions generate_smb3signingkey() and generate_smb3encryptionkey() expose sensitive cryptographic key material (session keys, signing keys, encryption/decryption keys) by printing their raw bytes through ksmbd_debug() when AUTH debugging is enabled.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes multiple ksmbd_debug(AUTH, ...) calls that used the %*ph format to dump the raw key buffers, such as "Session Key   %*ph\n" and "Signing Key   %*ph\n" in generate_smb3signingkey(), and similar dumps of encryption/decryption keys in generate_smb3encryptionkey().

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces generate_smb3signingkey() and generate_smb3encryptionkey() which print cryptographic key material via ksmbd_debug(AUTH, ...) with %*ph format. For example, in generate_smb3signingkey(): 'ksmbd_debug(AUTH, "Key generation, the generated key: %*ph\n", (int)enginelen, key);' and in generate_smb3encryptionkey(): 'ksmbd_debug(AUTH, "Key generation, the generated key: %*ph\n", (int)enginelen, encryption_key);' and similarly for decryption_key. These debug prints expose sensitive key bytes when AUTH debugging is enabled, matching the vulnerability root cause.
